The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) intends to award a single-award, Firm-Fixed-Price, Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract for Tier II Mobile Command Post Vehicle (MCPV) systems. The purpose of this acquisition is to establish a contract vehicle for the design, engineering, manufacturing, integration, testing, and production of trailer-based mobile command post systems capable of supporting FBI command, control, communications, and computer (C4) operations. The Tier II MCPV requirement consists of a custom-integrated gooseneck trailer system and, when ordered, a compatible Class 4 prime hauler vehicle. The MCPV Trailer shall provide a mobile operational environment supporting mission communications, networking, workspace, power generation and distribution, environmental control, equipment racks, audio/visual capabilities, RF and satellite connectivity provisions, security systems, and integration of Government-furnished and Contractor-furnished mission equipment. The contract will include a First Article requirement. The Contractor shall design, manufacture, integrate, test, and obtain Government approval of an initial MCPV Trailer configuration prior to production quantities. The approved First Article configuration will establish the production baseline for subsequent MCPV Trailer systems. The Government anticipates ordering approximately thirteen (13) MCPV trailer systems and associated prime hauler vehicles over the contract ordering period; however, the Government guarantees only the minimum contract obligation identified in the solicitation. The maximum contract value shall not exceed $15,000,000.00.

Projekto konkurso dalyviai turi pateikti memorialinio kūrinio meninę idėją, atspindinčią Klaipėdos miesto įkūrimo istoriją, miesto tapatybę ir istorinę atmintį. Projektas turi apimti memorialinio kūrinio meninius, architektūrinius ir techninius sprendinius, jo integravimą į pasirinktą vietą. Kartu turi būti pateikti memorialinio kūrinio vizualiniai, konstrukciniai, medžiagiškumo ir apšvietimo sprendiniai. Su projekto konkurso laimėtoju numatoma sudaryti paslaugų pirkimo–pardavimo sutartį (toliau – projekto (paslaugų pirkimo–pardavimo) sutartis) dėl memorialinio kūrinio projektavimo, pagaminimo, pastatymo ir kitų su projekto įgyvendinimu susijusių darbų atlikimo. Išsamus projekto konkurso objekto aprašymas ir memorialiniam kūriniui keliami reikalavimai pateikiami Techninėje specifikacijoje (konkurso sąlygų 4 priedas). Projekto konkurso tikslas – atrinkti meniškai vertingiausią, istoriškai pagrįstą ir urbanistiniame kontekste tinkamiausią memorialinio kūrinio idėją, skirtą Klaipėdos miesto įkūrėjų atminimui įamžinti ir Klaipėdos miesto istorinės atminties puoselėjimui. Biudžetas: Perkančioji organizacija informuoja, kad memorialinio kūrinio projektavimo, pagaminimo, transportavimo, montavimo bei kitų su projekto įgyvendinimu susijusių paslaugų bendra kaina negali viršyti šiam projekto konkursui skirtos maksimalios sumos – t. y. 123 966,94 Eur be PVM (jei tiekėjas yra ne PVM mokėtojas ar paslaugos neapmokestinamos PVM, ar dėl kitų priežasčių Perkančiosios organizacijos galutinė tiekėjui mokėtina suma bus be PVM) arba 150 000,00 Eur su PVM. Svarbu: jeigu dalyvio pasiūlyta kaina bus didesnė nei šiame punkte nustatyta maksimali kaina, projektas bus atmestas kaip neatitinkantis konkurso dokumentų reikalavimų pagal projekto konkurso sąlygų 64.3 p. Projekto konkurso pirmąsias 3 vietas užėmusius dalyvius numatyta apdovanoti piniginiais prizais (premijomis). Perkančioji organizacija laimėjusiu nustato tik 1 (vieną) dalyvį, surinkusį daugiausiai balų ir esantį pirmoje vietoje, neatitikusį pašalinimo pagrindų ir atitikusį nustatytus kvalifikacijos reikalavimus.

title: REPAIR LIVE FIRE TRAINING FACILITY AIRCRAFT MOCK-UP
description: The 910th Airlift Wing requires repair and corrective work to the Aircraft Fire Training Facility (AFTF) aircraft mock-up located at Youngstown Air Reserve Station. An inspection and evaluation of the Aircraft Fire Training Facility was conducted in August 2025 and finalized in April 2026. The assessment identified deficiencies affecting the facility's burner and ignition systems, structural components, corrosion protection, sprinkler system, propane distribution and emergency shutoff systems, control systems, and associated components. The contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, tools, transportation, testing, quality control, and other items and services necessary to complete the work identified in the Statement of Work, drawings, specifications, and solicitation attachments. Troubleshooting, repair, and/or replacement of the Tail Engine Burner, Wheel Well Burner, Flight Deck Burner, and Cargo Area Burner and associated ignition systems. Repair or replacement of burner ignition components as required to restore proper operation. Replacement of the malfunctioning cargo-area sprinkler head and restoration of proper drainage functionality. Structural steel repairs and corrosion remediation beneath portions of the aircraft mock-up. Corrosion repair beneath flight-deck stairs and around door assemblies. Repair and/or replacement of the warped R2 door and warped grating near the cargo-fire area. Certified welding and associated aircraft mock-up repairs. Installation/restoration of an emergency energy shutoff capability at the propane storage area. Installation of required solenoid valve(s) in the LPG/propane distribution system. Correction of deficiencies involving legacy pneumatic shutoff valves. Required control-system repairs/upgrades. Associated maintenance, testing, and corrective actions necessary to provide a complete and functional system. Applicable standards identified in the Government's technical documentation include, as applicable: USAF Technical Order 35E1-2-13-1 NFPA 54 NFPA 58 NFPA 70 NFPA 1003 NFPA 1402

title: Warehousing Support for CRSP
description: See attached Solicitation. Here is the PWS: Performance Work Statement (PWS): Centralized Receiving and Shipping Point (CRSP) The contractor shall provide Two (2) appropriately trained, supply and services labor to establish, operate, perform, and manage centralized receiving and shipping point (CRSP). Work hours are 0700 1530, Monday through Friday (30min lunch alternating). CRSP tasks include issuing to personnel authorized by delegation of authority card, DA Form 1687 (electronic or manual form acceptable) maintained on file, receiving, unloading or diverting trucks, reviewing manifests, breaking out items, inspecting items, recording transactions, receiving push shipments, redirecting mis-shipments, inspecting, photographing and coordinating with the Installation Transportation Division (ITD). The contractor shall operate the Automated Manifest System (AMS). The contractor shall perform these functions in accordance with AR 710-2, DA PAM 710-2-2 AR 735-5. The contractor shall use material handling, motor transportation to distribute cargo to, or receive cargo from, other CRSPs, ports operations areas, or bases/camps in support of onward movement and retrograde. The contractor shall distribute and backhaul supplies and materials to supply activities on the installation. The contractor shall maintain complete visibility of all ISO containers moving to and from the CRSP and provide input to the Army Container Asset Management System (ACAMS). The contractor shall provide monthly Labor Hours worked per Attachment 0002 Hours Work Report. The contractor shall submit documents per the Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) found in Attachments 0003 and 0004. Please note the contractor's Safety and Health Plan (CDRL 002) and Emergency Response Plan (CDRL 003) is due not later than (NLT) 60 days after contract award.

title: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement
description: Youghiogheny Resource Managers Building Siding Replacement. USACE, Pittsburgh District, has an upcoming requirement to replace the siding of the Resource Managers Office at Youghiogheny River Lake. The work described herein shall be performed at the Youghiogheny Resource Managers Office (RMO) building located within the Youghiogheny River Lake project area in Confluence, Pennsylvania. The building currently serves as administrative office space for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The RMO building was constructed in 1986 and is a multi-level, timber-framed structure built into the hillside overlooking the impoundment side of the dam. The exterior walls consist of 2x6 wood stud framing with 6-inch fiberglass batt insulation (R-19, foil-faced). Interior partitions consist of 2x4 wood studs with 1/2-inch gypsum wallboard. The existing exterior wall assembly consists of 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing with 5/8-inch cedar-faced T1-11 plywood siding, for a combined nominal thickness of 1-1/8 inches. Exterior trim and fascia consist of various widths of cedar lumber. The building is supported by cast-in-place concrete footings and 12-inch concrete masonry unit (CMU) foundation walls. The rear wall section and balcony framing are supported by 4 feet-0 inches wide by 5 feet-0 inches deep concrete footings, laminated wood columns (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches), and laminated wood beams (8-3/4 inches x 15 feet-0 inches).This project consists of the removal and replacement of the existing exterior wall cladding system. The Contractor shall remove and dispose of the existing T1-11 siding and 1/2-inch asphalt-saturated fibrous sheathing in their entirety. The Contractor shall furnish and install a new exterior wall assembly consisting of 1/2-inch APA-rated structural wood sheathing, a continuous weather-resistive barrier (WRB), 3/8-inch nominal preservative-treated wood furring strips, and 5/16-inch fiber cement lap siding in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The new wall assembly is intended to match the existing wall thickness (approximately 1-1/8 inches) to maintain alignment with existing window and door openings. Minor dimensional variation within normal construction tolerances are acceptable and shall not require modification or resetting of existing windows and doors. The Contractor shall not reset, relocate, or otherwise modify existing windows and doors. Furring strips shall be installed vertically over the WRB at a maximum spacing of 16 inches on center and shall be fastened through the sheathing into wall framing members. Fiber cement siding shall be installed horizontally over the furring strips and fastened through the furring and sheathing into wall framing members. Furring strips are intended to provide a drainage and ventilation cavity and shall not be used as the sole fastening substrate for the fiber cement lap siding. The Contractor shall ensure that all fiber cement lap siding edges are supported by framing members or approved blocking in accordance with manufacturer requirements. The Contractor shall furnish and install all required trim at windows, doors, corners, and transitions. Trim material shall be fiber cement. The cedar hand railing on the balconys is to be new capped PVC or capped composite decking of matching color to fiber cement board siding. The Contractor shall provide complete flashing at all required locations, including but not limited to head flashing at windows and doors, Z-flashing at horizontal joints and transitions, and kick-out flashing at roof-to-wall intersections. All flashing shall be integrated with the WRB in a shingle-lap manner to maintain a continuous drainage plane. The work shall be completed within 180 after written Notice to Proceed. description: This solicitation is for commercial items and has been prepared in accordance with the format outlined in FAR Subpart 12.6, supplemented with additional information contained in this notice. Navy Paint Warranty: Paint, coatings, and preservation products must meet the required standards per the attached Navy Paint Warranty (Attachment 3). OEM Certification: Offerors must provide proof of Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) certification for the paint and coating systems. Personnel may not be substituted without express written approval by the Government. Hull Coating System: Provide a twelve (12) year antifouling, underwater hull, and boot top coating system that complies with epoxy anticorrosive MIL-PRF-24647, Type I or II, and that complies with antifouling paint MIL-PRF-24647, Type II. Marking Compatibility: Provide preservation products that are suitable for use as hull and boot top markings on the ablative antifoulant paints. Substrate Compatibility: All preservation products must be compatible and have the ability to be applied over any existing coating on like surfaces. Statutory and Licensing Requirements Homeport Statute (10 U.S.C. 7299A): In accordance with the "Homeport Statute", this procurement will solicit offers only from offerors capable of performing the work in the Mayport homeport area. Agreement for Boat Repair (ABR): Offerors must have, or be able to obtain, an Agreement for Boat Repair (ABR) or Government-approved equivalency by the time of contract award. Summary of Navy Paint Warranty (Attachment 3) The successful contractor will be required to provide an express Marine Coatings Warranty (incorporated into FAR 52.212-4(o) Addendum) that includes: Two-Year Application Durability: Warranting that the paint is applied correctly so that it lasts a minimum of two (2) years after the date of application, and that the paint is usable up to its expiration date. Hull Scamping: Providing scamping of the underwater hull at no cost to the Government if more than twenty (20) percent of the underwater hull is heavily fouled due to poor performance of the antifouling within two (2) years of application. description: En 2021, la Comisión Europea lanzó la estrategia de inversiones Global Gateway, que tiene como objetivo fomentar inversiones de gran calibre en infraestructura verde y digital en los países socios, con soluciones innovadoras y de calidad, creando al mismo tiempo valor añadido local y promoviendo el crecimiento económico, el empleo y la cohesión social. Durante la III Cumbre UE-CELAC, celebrada en julio de 2023, los dirigentes de ambas regiones reafirmaron su compromiso de reforzar la asociación birregional, reconociendo la importancia de la Agenda de Inversiones Global Gateway. Dicho compromiso fue renovado durante la IV Cumbre UE-CELAC celebrada en noviembre de 2025. El objetivo general de esta acción es contribuir a la implementación de inversiones sostenibles y transformadoras en los sectores de transición verde y digital en Guatemala, donde haya un interés común europeo y de la agenda de desarrollo de Guatemala, y ello en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway, asegurando su alineación con las prioridades estratégicas del país y fomentando un desarrollo inclusivo y sostenible. title: Unlocking Commercial and Industrial Captive Renewable Energy in Uganda: Market Sizing and Regulatory Reform
description: The UK Government's Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions (UK PACT) programme is inviting proposals from qualified suppliers or consortia to deliver technical assistance to Uganda's Electricity Regulatory Authority (ERA). Uganda's electricity sector is predominantly powered by renewable energy and demand is growing rapidly. However, uptake of commercial and industrial (C&I) captive renewable energy remains limited due to regulatory gaps, insufficient market data, and barriers to investment. This is particularly significant given the growing role of behind-the-meter renewable energy as a means of reducing diesel reliance, improving energy security, and supporting economic growth. The assignment will support ERA, in partnership with the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development (MEMD) and electricity distributors UEDCL, WENRECO and KIS, to strengthen the enabling environment for C&I captive renewable energy. The work will establish an evidence base on market demand, existing captive generation and grid capacity, review Uganda's regulatory framework and international best practice, and develop targeted regulatory and market-enabling solutions. Key outputs are expected to include recommendations for a mid-tier regulatory framework, updated settlement and implementation guidance, standardised commercial documentation, and financing pathways to improve project bankability. The project aims to increase private-sector investment in captive renewable energy, accelerate deployment, reduce dependence on diesel generation, and strengthen Uganda's energy security and grid resilience. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk
